# Standards & federation

Thematiq declares the standards below in its manifest. OpenRegister publishes them to other servers without login, under `thematiq.discovery` in `/ocs/v2.php/cloud/capabilities`, so another instance can tell from a hostname alone whether it can connect. Tools such as [Nextcloud Peek](https://genhttp.dev/lambda/nextcloud-peek/) show it too.

## Standards this app provides

| Standard | Version | Access | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| [NL Design System design tokens (CSS custom properties per token set)](https://nldesignsystem.nl/) | — | Public | — |
| [W3C Design Tokens Format (import and export)](https://www.designtokens.org/) | 2025.10 | Nextcloud login | — |
| [WCAG contrast evaluation of token pairs](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/) | 2.1 | Nextcloud login | — |

## Standards this app uses

None.

## Federation (Open Cloud Mesh)

Thematiq registers no Open Cloud Mesh resource type of its own. Objects it stores in OpenRegister can still be shared with another instance through OpenRegister's `openregister` resource type.

## How another server finds this

```bash
curl -s -H 'OCS-APIRequest: true' \
  'https://cloud.example.org/ocs/v2.php/cloud/capabilities?format=json' \
  | jq '.ocs.data.capabilities["thematiq"].discovery'
```

Paths are relative to the instance root. Prefix `/index.php` when the instance runs without pretty URLs (`core.mod-rewrite-working` is false). Endpoints that need a Nextcloud login are listed without their path.

## Administrators

- Stop publishing discovery for every app: `occ config:app:set openregister discovery_public --value=no`
- Hide only this app: add `thematiq` to `occ config:app:set openregister discovery_hidden_apps --value=...` (comma separated)

Field reference and the shared list of standard ids: [Discovery and federation](https://github.com/ConductionNL/openregister/blob/development/docs/Technical/discovery-and-federation.md).
